text_excerpt: Pro tip: Go early (8:00 a.m.) during the weekend to avoid long lines. Totes worth it, even if you're hungover. My friend and I ate breakfast here on our way out of NOLA. I got the ham po'boy. I know, I know, it's pretty tame, but after several days of heavy Cajun cuisine, I was really looking forward to something a little more...plain. And while it was a cold cut sandwich, essentially, it was quite stellar. Great bread, great dressing, and a nice portion. My friend had the Cajun omelet with grit

Came to Mother's when I visited New Orleans with my friends - one of whom is a Louisiana and New Orleans native. He brought us to Mother's after a night of hard partying in the French Quarter. There was a bit of a line but it was worth the wait (we went and ordered their bloody Mary's and waited in line with them). What a great dining experience here overall. We could not wait to try an Emeril restaurant! We had a reservation here for Friday night at 9:00pm that we almost didn't make it to. Gladly, two out of three of us made it there after an intense day of day drinking. I wanted so many things on the menu, but my eyes were bigger than my stomach.. so I had to cut down. We started with the Charred Kale Salad - after everything we have been eating in NOLA, I think it's safe to say that we need some greens.

I have to say I have always been at least a little bit smitten by Emeril Despite all his "bams!", which are annoying, I've always found him charming and adorable...or maybe it's just that New Bedford accent and his New England ties that have drawn me in. During my previous New Orleans trip, I met a woman in a wine shop who told me she and her husband would be forever grateful to Emeril. Everything came out really fast too. The wine and drink selection is nice and tbh the glass of Riesling I had was probably the best glass I've ever had. Jennifer was our guide and she was amazing. She made the tour fun and she knew tons of interesting facts and information about the city and it's past. Our tour guide Ryan was an incredibly captivating storyteller, so much so that I was totally spooked out and couldn't sleep that night! This was honestly one of those experiences that I know I'll remember for the rest of my life, as well as how much fun I had hanging out and getting scared with my friends. We did the voodoo, vampire, witches tour. We had Edward as our guide. He was awesome! Friendly and informative. We checked in 10 min before start time. I think arriving 30 min prior is too long. We stopped at 4 places and he talked about the history and stories. Some of the stories were frightening. In the middle we stopped at a bar if we needed to us the restroom. I noticed towards the end of the tour our group got smaller, oh well. Overall, great tour and experience.

This was our first time in NOLA and per some recommendations from back home, we decided to get brunch at Ruby Slipper. It was a great first meal! *** Tip: Put yourself on Yelp wait list as it gets pretty packed *** I got the Grilled fish St. Peter and my girlfriend got the Peacemaker (chose 2 different egg benedicts). My meal was delicious and definitely one of my favorites during our trip. The fish was cooked perfectly and seasoned just right. The egg benedicts were pretty good as well. Service

It was really nice out so it was nice to sit outside. The table was super sticky though which was a little uncomfortable at times.
